panels.title: Learning with 3% labels
panels.subtitle: 15 clients · 100 rounds · accuracy (%)
panels.finding: With 3% labels, +23.84 accuracy points on Speech Commands; smaller gains on the other tasks.

panels.title: Does pretraining always help?
panels.subtitle: Speech Commands · 50% unlabeled pool · 100 rounds
panels.finding: Pretraining improves the endpoint at 20% and 50% labels, but not at 3% or 5%.

takeaways: Unlabeled audio helps all three selected 3%-label comparisons.
Initialization gains depend on the label budget; pretraining is not uniformly better after 100 rounds.

notes: All 14 displayed numeric cells were checked against the final publisher PDF table renders and extracted table text. Source is the final ACM TECS 21(6), Article 74 (2022) version, not the earlier cached manuscript.
Preserve each mean and printed ± term verbatim. Appendix captions call the terms variance across experiments; do not relabel them SD or CI, convert their units, or plot invented error intervals.
Speech Commands gain is derived from Table 9: 86.82 - 62.98 = 23.84 percentage points. The three dataset accuracies are separate tasks and are not averaged.
Table 7 uses 15 clients, q=80%, sigma=25%, beta=0.5 and E=1. The selected U=50% slice avoids the conflicting U=100%, L=5% mean in main Table 6 versus Appendix Table 7.
The pretraining panel compares the 100-round endpoint, not Figure 6 early convergence. No result-data correction was needed.
